findings.title: Rejected device is cached before the store call, so a retry bypasses the limit
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. If the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the key stays cached for 29 minutes. The next request from the same rejected device hits the cache at line 83, returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` lets the request through as an anonymous user. A rejected device is therefore blocked once and then allowed for the rest of the cache TTL, which defeats the feature. The cache key should only be set after a successful store call, or removed when the store returns an error.

findings.title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic and can overshoot under concurrency
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices`, compares it with `deviceLimit`, and then does a separate upsert, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent first requests from many new devices, or from several Grafana instances in HA, can all see `count < limit` and all insert. The configured limit can then be exceeded by roughly the request concurrency. If the limit is meant to be hard, the check and insert need to be atomic (for example a conditional INSERT ... SELECT with the count in the same statement, or a transaction/lock). If it is meant to be soft, the docs should say so.

findings.title: Limit error is a plain error, so rejected users get an unhelpful generic auth failure
findings.body: When the limit is hit, `Authenticate` returns the bare `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which is created with `fmt.Errorf` and carries no HTTP status or public message. The authn layer treats it as a generic authentication failure, so the user sees an opaque 401 or a redirect to login rather than a message that the anonymous device limit was reached. Using a typed error such as an `errutil` Unauthorized or Forbidden with a public message would give a deterministic status code and a useful message.

findings.title: Device tagging is now synchronous on the request path and uses the request context
findings.body: The previous fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout context is replaced by a blocking `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call. Every anonymous request that misses the local cache now waits on a COUNT query plus an upsert before authentication completes. If the request context is cancelled, the tagging fails. Synchronous behaviour is needed to enforce the limit, but it adds DB latency and a DB dependency to the auth path. Reviewers should be aware of this, and the tradeoff should be applied only when `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`.

findings.title: No test covers the limit-reached path through the service or client
findings.body: The only new test is the store-level `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`. Nothing tests `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` or `Anonymous.Authenticate` with a limit set. That means nothing exercises that the error propagates, that a rejected device is not cached, or that other tag errors are still only logged. A test of this kind would have caught the cache-before-store bug in `tagDeviceUI`.

findings.title: New `device_limit` option under [auth.anonymous] is undocumented
findings.body: `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is read here, but `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini` and the configuration docs are not updated. Operators cannot discover the option, nor that 0 means unlimited. The PR description is also left as the unfilled template.
